notes:
Account overview: Kairos builds low-latency personalization and trading signals for retail brokers. Heavy emphasis on sub-50ms P95 inference for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and predictable cost per 1M requests. Team is ops-heavy — SRE + infra + ML engineers (primary contact: VP Eng, Clara Hu).

Sales/Eng sync notes (02/11 demo):
- Demoed Redwood Dedicated; showed autoscale and canary rollout. Positive reaction to model pinning and fallback policy.
- Clara: 'We need tail latency guarantees; spikes kill our matching pipeline.'
- Primary interest: batching/caching knobs, quantization guidance (4-bit/llm.int8/awq), and perf benchmark harness.

Requirements (explicit):
- Latency: p95 <= 40ms for 128 tokens, p99 < 120ms under 200 QPS sustained.
- Throughput: baseline 400 QPS during market-open windows; burst to 1k QPS for 2-5 min windows.
- Cost sensitivity: target unit cost <= $0.002 per request (128-token baseline).
- Models: prefer open models (Llama-family, Mistral variants) but open to Redwood-verified variants + quantized artifacts.
- Routing/fallback: prefer region-based routing (NA primary, EU DR) + automatic fallback to smaller model on overload.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2/audit logs, KMS for key management, logs retention 1 year, EU data residency for subset of customers.

Evaluation plan / what they want from POC:
- 2-week Dedicated POC: simulate production traffic using their real request distribution (prefix distribution provided), Redwood to run perf matrix (latency, cost per token, GPU utilization) across quantization profiles, batching windows, cache hit rates.
- Deliverables: CSV perf matrix, recommended batching & cache policy, suggested quantization profile with expected accuracy delta by prompt class, rollback plan.

Timeline & recent activities:
- 2026-02-04: Intro call (AE Jordan + SE Maya) — discovered latency targets and compliance needs.
- 2026-02-11: Product demo + high-level perf discussion (ff-20260211-8241).

POC acceptance criteria (customer-defined):
- Meets p95 latency target for 128-token baseline at 400 QPS with <10% increase in p99 compared to baseline.
- Demonstrates >= 3x cost reduction vs their current hosted provider using batching+quantization without >5% accuracy regression on evaluation prompts.
- Integration tests: SSO SAML pass, KMS flow validated, logs ingestion to their SIEM.

Technical notes (from SE):
- Workload is latency-sensitive but highly repetitive prefix patterns — big win for prefix caching / KV cache. They expect 30-60% cache hit rate if caching is tuned.
- Batching: careful — microbatching with 4-8 request groupings reduces cost but may add latency tail; need continuous-batching experiment.
- Quantization: prefer AWQ/QLoRA-style 4-bit for 30-40% GPU memory reduction; must validate semantic regression on their TIE (test-in-eval) set.
- Benchmark plan: run controlled synthetic replay + shadow traffic ramp to measure tail latencies; gather per-token cost, kernel utilization, and KV hit/miss logs.

- Procurement: legal counterparty review timeline unknown (security package attached in drive).
- Billing model: want committed monthly cap + burst pricing for market-open; Redwood to propose pricing table.
- GPU quota: customer may require Dedicated pool <-> region capacity reservation; check infra availability for requested dates (May POC start).
